title: Studio
description: Ask the agent for a change in plain words, and watch the project change live next to the conversation.

restricted.title: For the server's administrators
restricted.description: The Studio is open to the server's administrators for now.

setup.agentTitle: The Studio has no agent server
setup.description: Turn it on and name the service that runs its OpenHands agent server, in Settings, Studio.
setup.memberOffDescription: An administrator of this server can turn it on.

list.emptyTitle: No project in the Studio yet
list.emptyDescription: Add a project from GitHub: the Studio copies it for the agent, makes its live preview and opens it.
list.emptyNoFolder: Set the projects folder in the Studio's settings to add projects from GitHub, or link a service that already shows a project's preview.
list.memberEmptyTitle: No project shared with you yet
list.memberEmptyDescription: Once an administrator shares a project with you, it shows here: open it to talk to the agent and see it live.

link.title: Link a project to the Studio
link.description: The Studio shows the service's live preview, and the agent works on the project's folder.
link.serviceHint: The service whose container shows the project's live preview.
link.folderHint: The project's folder as the agent server sees it, such as /projects/my-project.
link.folderRequired: Enter an absolute path, starting with /.

conversation.label: Conversation
conversation.waiting: The agent is waiting for a confirmation.
conversation.emptyDescription: Describe it in plain words, or paste a screenshot. The agent changes the code, and the preview on the right follows.
conversation.readOnly: This conversation happened with the agent shared by every project. The project has its own agent now: start a new conversation to go on.
conversation.agentAsleep: The project's agent is resting. Send a message, or open the project again, to wake it.

composer.label: Message to the agent
composer.placeholder: Reply to the agent… Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line.
composer.imageFailed: This image could not be read.
composer.elementPlaceholder: What should change in this element?

preview.label: Live preview
preview.open: Open the preview in a new tab
preview.startingDescription: It usually takes about fifteen seconds.
preview.stoppedDescription: Start it to see the project here.
preview.undeployedDescription: It has never run: its first start builds it, which takes a minute or two.
preview.noAddressDescription: Give its service a domain, then come back.
preview.inspectUnavailable: This preview does not load the Studio's inspector
preview.inspecting: Click an element of the preview to join it to your message. Esc cancels.

settings.title: Studio
settings.description: The Studio lets someone talk to an OpenHands agent about a project and see the result live. The panel reaches the agent server from inside its service's container, so the server needs no domain, and its key stays in its container.
settings.enabledHint: It shows in the top bar for the server's administrators.
settings.serviceHint: The service that runs the OpenHands agent server.
settings.urlHint: Where the agent server listens inside its container, on 127.0.0.1.
settings.keyFileHint: Where the agent server keeps its key, in its container. Not needed when the key is in SESSION_API_KEY.
settings.checkOk: The panel reaches the agent server, version {{version}}.
settings.checkFailed: The panel does not reach the agent server: {{message}}
settings.projectsDirHint: Where projects go in the agent server's container, such as /projects. It must be a folder of the server mounted in that service, from its Storage tab: each project added is copied there, and its preview mounts the same folder.
settings.previewSignInHint: Each preview asks for the panel's own account instead of the password the server shares with every site: the server's administrators and the accounts its project is shared with get in, nobody else. The panel and the previews should share a domain, as panel.example.com and the previews' *.example.com do, for the preview to open inside the Studio.
settings.agentPerProjectHint: Each project gets its own agent server, in an Opsifier project of its own with its preview: it sees only its project's folder, reaches no other service, and holds no GitHub token, since the panel passes its git to its repository. It starts when the project is opened and stops when nobody uses it. The service above becomes the model each one is copied from: its image, settings and models, never its secrets.
settings.isolateTitle: Projects still on the shared agent
settings.isolateDescription_one: {{count}} project still works with the shared agent, and waits for its own. Its conversations so far stay readable, and its preview so far is stopped and kept where it is, for you to remove.
settings.isolateDescription_other: {{count}} projects still work with the shared agent, and wait for their own. Their conversations so far stay readable, and their previews so far are stopped and kept where they are, for you to remove.
settings.isolateAction: Give each project its own agent
settings.isolateDone_one: {{count}} project has its own agent now.
settings.isolateDone_other: {{count}} projects have their own agent now.

starters.design: Give the home page a more modern look
starters.mobile: Make the site pleasant on a phone
starters.texts: Read the texts and fix the typos

element.label: Element pointed at in the preview

add.title: Add a GitHub project
add.description: The Studio copies the repository with the agent server's GitHub token, makes its live preview, and opens it. The agent then pushes its changes to the repository.
add.repositoryHint: Its address, such as https://github.com/owner/name, or owner/name. The agent server's GitHub token must reach it, with Contents in read and write.
add.branchHint: The branch the agent works on and pushes to. The repository's default branch when left empty.
add.working: Copying the repository and making its preview… This can take a minute.
add.done: {{name}} is in the Studio. Its preview is starting: the first start installs its dependencies.

share.title: Share {{name}}
share.description: Each account ticked sees this project in the Studio, its conversations and its live preview, and nothing else of the server.
share.none: No member account yet. Invite the designers from Settings, Accounts, as members with no project: they will appear here.
share.admins: The server's administrators see every project already.

remove.title: Delete {{name}} from the Studio?
remove.description: Its conversations, its shares, its agent and its preview are deleted, with the Opsifier project the Studio made for it. Its folder stays on the server, with any work not pushed: adding the same repository again picks it up. A site linked to the Studio stays, without the Studio's sign-in in front of it.

githubKeys.title: GitHub keys
githubKeys.description: A fine-grained token reaches the repositories of one account or organization only. Give the Studio one for each owner whose repositories it works on: a project with an agent server of its own is copied, and its agent's git passed to GitHub, with the key of its repository's owner. Without one, or when GitHub refuses it, the agent server's GITHUB_TOKEN secret serves. Agents never see a token.
githubKeys.none: No key yet: the agent server's GITHUB_TOKEN secret serves every repository it reaches.
githubKeys.checked: GitHub knows this token: it is {{login}}'s.
githubKeys.checkFailed: GitHub did not accept this token.
githubKeys.removeDescription: Its repositories fall back on the agent server's GITHUB_TOKEN secret, when it reaches them. Projects whose repositories it does not reach can no longer pull or push.
githubKeys.addDescription: On GitHub, Settings, Developer settings, Fine-grained tokens: choose the owner as resource owner, the repositories, and Contents in read and write.
githubKeys.ownerHint: The account or organization, as in github.com/voidagency/mcp-checkmate.
githubKeys.tokenHint: Kept sealed on the server, and never shown again.
githubKeys.replacedDone: The key of {{owner}} has its new token
githubKeys.refused: GitHub refused this token at the last check
githubKeys.noRepositories: {{login}}'s token reads no private repository of {{owner}}: check its resource owner and its repositories on GitHub.
githubKeys.ownOnly: GitHub keys serve projects that have an agent server of their own: turn on « One agent per project » to use them.
